system_description.narrative_title: Fractured global order: Iran conflict, AI boom, and supply‑chain strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, tightly coupled and rapidly changing field where regional kinetic conflicts (notably US–Iran and Russia–Ukraine), a market‑transforming AI and tech build‑out, and trade/energy choke‑point pressures interact and amplify one another. U.S. threats of unprecedented economic measures and a potential indefinite naval blockade of Iran are disrupting oil flows, shipping and markets while prompting fiscal and monetary interventions. At the same time an AI infrastructure and financing surge is reshaping capital markets, corporate strategy and labour markets, even as China reroutes trade (Arctic corridors, export push) and faces domestic job stress. These overlapping stressors make shocks in energy, finance, and security prone to cross‑contaminate across regions and sectors.
system_description.scope: State and non‑state security operations and alliances, maritime chokepoints and shipping routes, global energy and commodity flows, international financial markets and central bank interventions, AI and high‑tech industrial and supply‑chain ecosystems, major national economic and trade policies
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic system (the integrated international order encompassing geopolitics, global markets, and transnational supply chains)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime chokepoints (Hormuz, Black Sea, Panama Canal)
International financial markets and central bank policy
AI and high‑tech industrial / semiconductor ecosystem
Regional security complexes (Middle East, Eastern Europe, East Asia)

variables.name: U.S.–Iran strategic confrontation
variables.description: United States, Iran and Gulf states; the US is escalating unprecedented economic pressure and naval coercion while Iran pushes back through maritime attacks and deeper regional and financial alignments.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine with Western backers; the war remains intense with sustained strikes, drone and missile campaigns and growing strain on Ukrainian defenses and allied weapons supplies.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: United States and China; accelerating state-led competition via tariffs, export controls and industrial policy is reshaping global supply chains for semiconductors and advanced technologies.

variables.name: AI-driven economic and systemic shift
variables.description: Global tech powers, investors and regulators; an AI-led boom in compute demand, leveraged financing and novel cyber risks is reconfiguring capital allocation, labour markets and systemic market vulnerabilities.

variables.name: Global shipping and energy chokepoints
variables.description: Global trading states and maritime actors; conflict, extreme weather and capacity shortfalls are disrupting key maritime routes (canals, straits and polar passages), rerouting trade and lifting logistics and energy costs.
